title: Test complete accounting for every TX traffic class
description:
Scope: complete-emission traffic-class cases in the admission supplement under /home/mark/Developer/lichen-workspace/project-LICHEN/test/vectors/. Enumerate control, data, forwarding, retries, signed headers and applicable experimental parity costs against shared frequency/group and legal/adaptive accounts. Derive full PHY lengths and airtime independently from the frozen arithmetic, not application bytes or production counters. Keep unsupported experimental emission disabled; hypothetical accounting records do not authorize an on-air experiment or alter baseline framing/SCHC.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Reuse vectors.06 airtime and vectors.09 ledger arithmetic; add only a bounded traffic-matrix case group. Distinguish emitted airtime from setup or listening time.
acceptance_criteria: Independent frame-length and emission ledgers include every actual wrapper, signature, retry and forwarding emission in the appropriate accounts. No control, priority, fallback or SOS class gains an unconfigured exemption. Hypothetical parity/header traffic is either correctly accounted under an explicitly permitted test configuration or rejected as unsupported; it never enables a baseline mode. All expected totals and denials are exact, schema-validated and assigned to actual path-consumer cases.
